source: Comprehensive FRAC Fungicide Directory, Modes of Action & Resistance Management (Section 1)
text:
Section 1: Principles of Fungicide Resistance Management. The Fungicide Resistance Action Committee (FRAC) classifies chemical and biological active ingredients by their target biochemical site of action. Repeated application of single-site fungicides (e.g. FRAC 11 QoIs or FRAC 3 DMIs) exerts intense selective pressure, driving selection of resistant mutant subpopulations. To prevent resistance development:
1. Tank-mix or alternate single-site systemic fungicides with multi-site contact protectants (FRAC Group M). 2. Never exceed 2 sequential applications of a single FRAC group before rotating to an unrelated target site. 3. Strictly adhere to label Pre-Harvest Intervals (PHI) and Maximum Residue Limits (MRL). Section 2: The Comprehensive FRAC Code Classification:
1. FRAC Group M (Multi-Site Contact Protectants - Low Resistance Risk):
 - FRAC M01 (Inorganic Copper: copper octanoate, copper sulfate, copper hydroxide): Non-specific binding to fungal protein thiol groups. Bactericidal against Xanthomonas and Pseudomonas. - FRAC M02 (Inorganic Elemental Sulfur: micronized wettable sulfur): Multi-site disruptor of mitochondrial respiratory electron transport. Highly active on Powdery Mildew (Podosphaera) and mites. Phytotoxic above 30°C. - FRAC M03 (Dithiocarbamates: Mancozeb, Maneb): Inactivates sulfhydryl groups in enzymes. Excellent protectant tank-mix partner.

Excellent protectant tank-mix partner. - FRAC M04 (Phthalimides: Captan, Folpet): Thiol-reacting enzyme inhibitor. Core apple scab protectant. 2. FRAC Group 7 (SDHI - Succinate Dehydrogenase Inhibitors):
 - Active Ingredients: Boscalid, fluxapyroxad, fluopyram, penthiopyrad. - Biochemical Target: Complex II (succinate dehydrogenase) in the mitochondrial respiration chain. High-potency translaminar activity against Botrytis, Alternaria, and powdery mildews. Moderate to high resistance risk. 3. FRAC Group 3 (DMI - Demethylation Inhibitors / Triazoles):
 - Active Ingredients: Difenoconazole, myclobutanil, propiconazole, tebuconazole, prothioconazole. - Biochemical Target: Sterol 14alpha-demethylase (encoded by CYP51), inhibiting ergosterol biosynthesis in true fungal membranes. Systemic curative and preventative activity. Resistance mechanism is multi-step (CYP51 overexpression or point mutations). 4. FRAC Group 11 (QoI - Quinone Outside Inhibitors / Strobilurins):
 - Active Ingredients: Azoxystrobin, pyraclostrobin, trifloxystrobin. - Biochemical Target: Cytochrome b Qo site (Complex III) in mitochondrial respiration. High resistance risk driven by a single qualitative point mutation (G143A amino acid substitution). Never spray during Fusarium Head Blight (triggers DON toxin surge).

 - Active Ingredients: Mandipropamid, dimethomorph. - Biochemical Target: Cellulose synthase (CesA3) in Oomycetes. Ineffective on true fungi; highly specific for Phytophthora and Downy Mildew. 6. FRAC Group 44 (Microbial Biological Lipopeptides):
 - Active Ingredients: Bacillus amyloliquefaciens (strain D747), Bacillus subtilis (strain QST 713). - Biochemical Mode of Action: Synthesize cyclic lipopeptides (surfactins, iturins, and fengycins) that insert into fungal membranes and form pore channels, causing osmotic burst. Zero chemical residues, 0-day PHI, OMRI-listed organic. 7. FRAC Group P / P01 (Host Plant Defense Inducers):
 - Active Ingredients: Salicylic acid, acibenzolar-S-methyl (ASM), laminarin, potassium silicate. - Biochemical Mode of Action: Primes plant innate Systemic Acquired Resistance (SAR) without direct antimicrobial activity.
